ops-dev-control-plane.quote: never shares production state, transport credentials, merge authority or deployment authority

ops-backup-set.quote: Back up one consistent recovery set:

ops-recoverable-secret.quote: recoverable secret material: either encrypted credential ciphertext plus a separately escrowed/rotatable recovery key

ops-backup-coordinator.quote: The backup coordinator acquires a short snapshot lease

ops-objectives.quote: Initial acceptance objectives are RPO <= 5 minutes for durable control state and RTO <= 30 minutes on the same class of host.

ops-artifact-rpo.quote: Artifact RPO may vary by class but must be declared.

ops-restore-drill.quote: The drill verifies database integrity, manifests, artifact hashes, policy versions and startup in disconnected recovery mode before any transport lease can be acquired.

ops-credential-resolution.quote: Until required credentials resolve and their audiences/tenants are revalidated, transport intake, outbox delivery, provider starts and connector sends remain disabled.

ops-credential-descriptor.quote: Each credential records owner, purpose, audience, creation, expiry/rotation deadline and health state without exposing its value.

ops-credential-storage.quote: Prefer systemd credentials, protected descriptors or a host secret provider over copying long-lived secrets into child environments.

ops-rotation.quote: Rotation supports an overlap window and canary; revocation immediately disables new work and invalidates derived capabilities where possible.

ops-connector-credentials.quote: Each credential is bound to a connector installation and tenant

ops-secret-sources.quote: Secret-source adapters for systemd/local encryption, 1Password, Bitwarden and pinned command helpers return sealed descriptors

ops-credential-pools.quote: Credential pools group only accounts explicitly approved to share tenant, billing and data-boundary policy

ops-retention-fields.quote: Every class specifies owner, default TTL, maximum size, redaction, export eligibility, legal hold and deletion method.

ops-retention-relative.quote: Preview deltas and raw provider records have shorter defaults than authoritative business/audit records.

ops-deletion.quote: Deletion first removes access, records a tombstone, cancels future publication and then garbage-collects unreferenced bytes/backups according to policy.

ops-admission.quote: The scheduler applies policy before queue insertion and again before host start:

ops-admission-rejection.quote: Admission rejection is explicit and durable: rejected, deferred-until, or waiting-capacity.

ops-runbooks-runtime.quote: Ship redacted diagnostic bundles and runbooks for stuck leases, corrupt database/spool, disk exhaustion, provider outage, invalid schema, orphan host, poisoned outbox, failed handoff, failed rollback, credential expiry, artifact quarantine, kernel enforcement loss, stuck sandbox namespace/cgroup, egress-broker outage, denied dependency fetch, external-daemon attestation mismatch and sandbox-launcher failure.

ops-diagnostics-read-only.quote: Diagnostic creation is read-only and audited.

ops-runbooks-selfhost.quote: Runbooks cover clean-host SH0 bootstrap, source/toolchain acquisition failure, non-reproducible rebuild, superseded source, stuck build queue, candidate crash loop, failed self-host reload, candidate boundary violation, independent-builder outage, stale promotion plan, compromised development credential/trust root and stable development-state recovery.

ops-no-adhoc-repair.quote: No runbook repairs self-host state with ad hoc database edits.

ops-bootstrap-runbook.quote: runbook covers inspect/plan without mutation, exact start confirmation, status/attach, restart/resume, disk-pressure stop, failed handoff, cleanup preview and state export.

ops-bootstrap-registration.quote: Its runtime directories and repository worktrees are registered explicitly; cleanup never follows unresolved variables or removes unrelated source/user state.

ops-maintenance-modes.quote: Transitions are revisioned actions with visible reason, actor and expiry.

ops-selfhost-recovery.quote: Recovery keeps the last known-good seed/bootstrap verifier, exact corresponding source and dependency locks, plus an independently checksummed disconnected-start bundle.

ops-release-credentials-excluded.quote: Private release-signing, protected-branch and deployment credentials are never part of candidate or ordinary lab recovery.

ops-dev-provider-credentials.quote: Development provider credentials are audience-bound to stable or candidate identities

ops-candidate-retention.quote: Candidate retention is state-based: active/promotable and last-known-good artifacts are protected

goals-service-owner.quote: one service owner, one durable authority and no branding-driven ID rewrite

goals-platform-roles.quote: Platform roles, handles, emails and display names never imply an Automonique role.

goals-external-identity.quote: External identities resolve to durable actors and tenants before authorization

goals-artifact-store.quote: Attachments and generated files enter a content-addressed artifact store with digest, size, media type, provenance, tenant, visibility and retention policy.

goals-artifact-materialization.quote: Workspaces receive artifacts by explicit materialization; providers never receive arbitrary host paths from a client payload.

goals-artifact-service.quote: Inbound and outbound files cross the artifact service; platform download URLs/tokens never reach execution hosts.

goals-visibility-classes.quote: Raw provider records, reasoning-sensitive data and client-published reports have distinct visibility and retention classes.

goals-sandbox-budgets.quote: CPU, memory, PID, I/O, runtime, scratch, workspace, spool and artifact budgets are bounded and observable.

goals-admission.quote: Admission is tenant-, actor-, workspace- and provider-aware; concurrency, rate and cost budgets are enforced before a claim.

goals-generation-isolation.quote: Stable and candidate generations use distinct state, sockets, process identities, credentials, workspaces, artifacts, leases and outboxes

goals-backup-set.quote: A backup is a consistent recovery set: database, artifact manifests/objects, encrypted configuration, independently recoverable credential path, release manifest and workspace metadata.

goals-media-consent.quote: Voice, vision, image, video, browser and computer-use inputs and outputs enter through the artifact and consent model with bounded capture and retention.

state-actors.quote: actors are tenant-scoped principals; external Slack, Telegram, GitHub, Support and SDK identities are mapped explicitly

state-role-grants.quote: role grants and policy revisions are queryable historical records

state-approvals.quote: stores the immutable proposal/action revision, tenant, requesting actor, eligible approver policy, decision actor, transport evidence, expiry and terminal decision

state-workspaces.quote: registers tenant, canonical source, immutable base revision/snapshot, isolation kind, writable path token, lock state and lifecycle

state-external-uniqueness.quote: External identity uniqueness includes platform, application, external tenant/installation and immutable user ID.

state-attributes-not-authority.quote: Teams UPN/email/display name and Discord username/roles remain attributes, not keys or authority.

state-connector-installations.quote: binds platform application identity plus Microsoft tenant or Discord guild/user installation owner to exactly one Automonique tenant

state-secret-coordinates.quote: Interaction continuation tokens, webhook URLs and secret-bearing Teams service coordinates live in the credential store or short-retention encrypted records.

state-artifacts.quote: records content digest, size, media type, tenant, creator, provenance, visibility, retention class, encryption/key reference and storage locator

chan-discord-roles.quote: Guild roles and channel permissions may inform a policy mapping but never replace Automonique actor/role authorization.

tui-operator-role.quote: The server authenticates the Unix peer credentials and projects an operator role/capability set.

selfhost-dirty-builds.quote: Dirty development builds are allowed only in candidate namespaces and are never release-promotable.

selfhost-source-state.quote: Every build references a `SourceState` containing repository ID, worktree/base revision, tree digest, dirty patch digest, submodule/dependency locks, generated-source digest and changed paths.

verify-workspaces.quote: isolated workspaces, dirty-source snapshots, concurrent worktree locks and revision-checked promotion

gov-owner.quote: The owner selects work, chooses review depth from the change's risk, and alone
